newsitem.title: UK: UK's TransCo sells gas to balance low holiday use.
newsitem.headline: UK's TransCo sells gas to balance low holiday use.

text.p: The UK's public gas transporter TransCo, the pipeline arm of British Gas, carried 127 million cubic metres (mmcm) of gas on Monday, the company said today.

Monday, the August Bank Holiday in the UK except Scotland, was expected by some analysts to be the day of lowest gas use in the year. But in fact, on Sunday July 21 TransCo carried a mere 92.5 mmcm, less than 73 percent of yesterday's level.

UK natural gas consumption last year was 73.1 billion cubic metres, giving a notional daily rate of 200.3 mmcm a day. But there are wide seasonal variations in consumption. On February 20, TransCo carried its highest ever volume, 383 mmcm - over four times higher than the volume on the lowest day this year.

Because of the dearth of demand over the public holiday, TransCo sold gas on the flexibility market, its balancing mechanism, over the weekend. On Saturday, according to a spokesman, TransCo sold 11.05065 mmcm for 519,771 stg, while on Sunday it sold 7.763 mmcm for 345,157 stg.
